samples.summary: The backend v1 slides PUT re-implements the shared `bandBlockNumerics` walk instead of calling it, and the two copies already disagree
samples.evidence: This same change adds `bandBlockNumerics(blocks)` to `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts` and exports it from *both* docs entries (`src/index.ts`, `src/node.ts`) with a JSDoc that says it is the band "for the bodies that reach the same layout engine through a door with no attribute codec" and that its `columnWidths` rule is "the same rule the v1 slides `PUT` applies to a stored array". The controller nevertheless hand-rolls the identical walk in `bandSlideBlockNumerics` (style.lineHeight, listLevel, rowHeights, columnWidths+MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS), `bandSlideCellNumerics` (padding, colSpan/rowSpan) and the `fontSize` clamp inside `normalizeSlideInlines` (line 1206), plus its own private `asFiniteNumber` (line 1002) duplicating the one in numeric-attrs.ts. The controller already imports from `@wafflebase/docs`, so reuse was available. The copies are not equivalent today: `bandBlockNumerics` drops an inline image whose size fails `isPaintableImageSize`, while the PUT path never inspects `inline.style.image`, so a deck stored through the REST API keeps an out-of-band image that `YorkieSlidesStore.read()` then deletes — the write and read boundaries give two answers to the same question, which is exactly the divergence this change exists to close. Every future band added to one copy must be remembered in the other.

samples.summary: The DOCX importer band is scope the branch's own task record twice deferred to "its own change", and the record was not updated
samples.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md:165-170` (round 10) says: "Follow-up, not built here: the DOCX importer is an unaudited *producer* of the same bands. `docx-style-map.ts:50` writes `fontSize` straight from `<w:sz w:val>` … and `:148` writes `lineHeight = lineVal / 240` with no ceiling … Auditing and bounding an importer is its own change." Round 11 (line 242-244) repeats it as "Unchanged from round 10 and still deferred". This diff nonetheless bands exactly those two importer sites, and round 10's own summary (line 136-137) states "the numeric-hardening program is not extended to any new attribute". Neither the task doc nor any design doc is updated to record the reversal, so the branch's written scope decision and its code now disagree. The band itself is consistent with the reader bands, so the cost is record-keeping rather than behaviour.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` adds a new sanitization boundary on `root.stylesJson` that no design doc records, and it silently narrows the stored registry shape
samples.evidence: The new `sanitizeDocStyles` is wired into both registry read boundaries (`docsTreeToDocument` and `YorkieDocStore.readDocStyles`) and does more than band numbers: it deletes `inline.image`, reduces `inlineDark` to colour-only, and drops `inline`/`inlineDark`/`block` when stored as non-objects — a change to what the persisted `root.stylesJson` blob may express. `docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md` is the canonical doc for that blob (§ `root.stylesJson`, lines ~286-342) and contains no mention of banding or sanitization (grep for band|normalize|sanitiz|MAX_FONT_SIZE finds nothing), and the new prose in `docs/design/docs/docs.md` (lines 175-280) enumerates only `fontSize` / `lineHeight` / `padding` / image size at Tree-attribute boundaries plus the slides bodies — never the registry. The branch's task doc does not list it either. Per CONTRIBUTING, a data-shape/architecture change belongs in the canonical subsystem doc.

samples.summary: The new design-doc section states the bands are set at the editor's own control range, which the code it documents explicitly contradicts, and it omits the table-structure bands the change ships
samples.evidence: docs.md:222-223 reads "…and is set at the range the editor's own controls can produce, so nothing a gesture can make is altered." `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts` module header says the opposite and calls the distinction load-bearing: "Every band covers the range of every *producer* whose output we accept, not just the range this editor's own controls can reach", and sets `MAX_FONT_SIZE`/`MAX_LINE_HEIGHT` at Word/DrawingML ceilings while `FONT_SIZE_MAX` (the picker) stays at 400. The same doc section also omits the bands this change actually adds for table *structure* — `MAX_TABLE_SPAN`, `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS`, `MAX_COLUMN_RATIO`/`parseColumnWidthsAttr` — so the canonical record under-describes the shipped surface.

samples.summary: `applyListLevelChanges` is written three times (editor.ts, text-editor.ts, text-box-editor.ts) around the shared planner
samples.evidence: The plan itself is correctly centralised in `planListLevelChanges`, but the apply loop — `planListLevelChanges((fn) => forEachBlockInSelection(fn), delta)` followed by a `doc.setBlockType(id, 'list-item', { listKind, listLevel })` per change — is duplicated verbatim in `view/editor.ts` (~1636), `view/text-editor.ts` (`private applyListLevelChanges`) and `view/text-box-editor.ts` (~830). Only editor.ts's copy adds the `markDirty` step. In a repo whose stated expectation is reuse (and whose own task doc complains about four open-coded copies of the list-level clamp), the write half is the part that will next drift — e.g. a future `listKind` or dirty-marking rule has to be remembered in three places.
searchedFor: diff hunks for editor.ts / text-editor.ts / text-box-editor.ts applyListLevelChanges

samples.summary: One concept split across three model modules on a rationale that is false for one of them
samples.evidence: numeric-attrs.ts:8 justifies the split as "`listLevel` and a table's `rowHeights` have their own modules (`list-level.ts`, `row-height.ts`) because a gesture plans with them". `row-height.ts` contains only `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` and `normalizeRowHeight` — no planner and no gesture — so the stated reason does not apply to it, and the split costs three entries in both package entry points plus three new rows in the entry-parity allowlist. Folding `row-height.ts` into `numeric-attrs.ts` would leave one band module plus the gesture-bearing `list-level.ts`.
searchedFor: diff of row-height.ts, node.ts, index.ts, entry-parity.test.ts

samples.evidence: The new `walkCellsForSiblings` (document.ts:97) is a byte-for-byte twin of the adjacent `walkCellsForBlock` except for what it returns (`cell.blocks` vs the matching block), and `siblingBlocksOf` repeats `findBlock`'s three-region + parent-map + full-walk sequence. A single traversal returning `{ block, siblings }` would keep the two resolvers from drifting on nested-table handling.

finding.summary: The backend v1 slides PUT re-implements the shared `bandBlockNumerics` walk instead of calling it, and the two copies already disagree

The controller nevertheless hand-rolls the identical walk in `bandSlideBlockNumerics` (style.lineHeight, listLevel, rowHeights, columnWidths+MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS), `bandSlideCellNumerics` (padding, colSpan/rowSpan) and the `fontSize` clamp inside `normalizeSlideInlines` (line 1206), plus its own private `asFiniteNumber` (line 1002) duplicating the one in numeric-attrs.ts. The controller already imports from `@wafflebase/docs`, so reuse was available. The copies are not equivalent today: `bandBlockNumerics` drops an inline image whose size fails `isPaintableImageSize`, while the PUT path never inspects `inline.style.image`, so a deck stored through the REST API keeps an out-of-band image that `YorkieSlidesStore.read()` then deletes — the write and read boundaries give two answers to the same question, which is exactly the divergence this change exists to close. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. `bandBlockNumerics` is defined at packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:293 and exported from both docs entries (index.ts:112, node.ts:155), and its columnWidths comment (numeric-attrs.ts:343-348) explicitly cites "the same rule the v1 slides `PUT` applies to a stored array". The backend controller nevertheless re-implements that walk: bandSlideBlockNumerics (docs-content.controller.ts:1027-1057) repeats style.lineHeight, listLevel, rowHeights and the columnWidths slice(0, MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS)+normalizeColumnRatio??0 rule; bandSlideCellNumerics (:1060-1077) repeats padding and colSpan/rowSpan; normalizeSlideInlines (:1206) repeats the fontSize clamp; and asFiniteNumber (:1002) duplicates numeric-attrs.ts:256. Reuse was plainly available — the controller already imports the same normalizers from '@wafflebase/docs' at :44-57. The two copies already disagree: bandBlockNumerics deletes an inline image failing isPaintableImageSize (numeric-attrs.ts:323-332), while the controller never touches inline.style.image (the only 'image' occurrences in that file, :749 and :1148, are prose), and the read boundary YorkieSlidesStore does band every text body via bandBlockNumerics (yorkie-slides-store.ts:502,510,529), whose own comment at :494 concedes the v1 PUT is "only one of the two writers". So a deck written through the REST API stores an out-of-band image that every reader silently drops — duplicated logic giving two answers to the same question, which is the `major` duplication/reuse case in this lens. No guard elsewhere reconciles them.
